title_en: Apple Flags Supply Constraints; Amazon Cloud Growth Eases AI Worries
title_zh: 苹果预警供应限制，亚马逊云增长缓解AI投资担忧
summary_zh: 苹果公司警告称，其最受欢迎的产品正面临严重的供应限制，导致股价盘后下跌逾7%，尽管季度营收增长16%。即将离任的CEO库克表示供应限制的核心问题是需求超出预期，尤其是iPhone和Mac销售强劲。苹果还提到关税退款使其毛利率提高2%，并计划将退款再投资于美国。与此同时，亚马逊云业务AWS增长37%，推动股价盘后上涨10%，尽管公司自由现金流为负，AI投资持续扩大。分析师认为亚马逊基础设施投资满足了市场需求，但对长期承诺表示担忧。两家科技巨头的业绩对比反映出投资者对供应链风险与AI机遇的不同反应。
reading_passage:
Apple CEO Tim Cook is this year being replaced in the role by John Ternus.

Apple spooked Wall Street on Thursday by warning it expected a "significant" hit from growing supply constraints for its most popular products.

Shares in the company fell in after-hours trading by more than 7%, even as it showed a 16% increase in revenue to $109b (£81b) thanks in part to unexpectedly high iPhone sales, and a 26% increase in profits to $29b.

Outgoing chief executive Tim Cook said while the impact of supply constraints had already shown up with the availability of Mac computers, it was expected to worsen and spread to affect iPhone and iPad products.

"We're seeing some very significant constraints currently with limited flexibility in the supply chain to remedy it," Cook said.

One of the supply constraints was in key chip components of Apple's products, the firm said.

Devices such as Macs and iPhones require microprocessors with "advanced nodes" - essentially computer chip technology that allows them to operate more quickly - most of which Apple has manufactured through TSMC, which is based in Taiwan.

However, Cook insisted that the core issue was unexpected demand, mainly for iPhone and Mac products. Sales of those products grew 22% and 25% respectively during the June quarter.

Earlier this year, Apple said its iPhone 17 was so in demand that its launch was the biggest in the company's history.

"This is not a regular supply issue, it's a demand forecast issue to be candid," Cook added. "We've got a quarter ahead where we'll be scrambling on the supply side."

Apple also noted that its gross margin, or the amount of money it keeps from every sale, was 2% larger than it otherwise would have been during the last three months because of tariff refunds. That would mean the company received roughly $1.1b in such refunds, according to calculations by the BBC.

Cook said Apple intended to "reinvest the tariff refunds into the US".

The company previously said, external it intended to put $600b toward building out more domestic manufacturing over the next four years. China is currently the largest manufacturer of Apple's products.

Cook also addressed Apple's impending public relaunch of Siri, an AI assistant that the company has seemingly struggled to make competitive in an era of proliferating AI chatbots from the likes of OpenAI and Anthropic.

While the new version of Siri AI is still in public beta, essentially a testing phase before broader release, Cook said it is part of "an enormous opportunity for Apple going forward in AI."

"The ability to run on device is also very strategic, and sort of a competitive weapon, if you will," Cook said.

He added that negotiations with authorities in the European Union about releasing the new version of Siri are ongoing with the goal of making it available "to everyone, everywhere at the same time."

Investors proved less concerned with Amazon's future performance, pushing the company's stock up 10% in after hours trading.

Despite showing free cash flow of negative $7.6bn due to massive and ongoing spending on AI projects, Amazon's core businesses grew enough to offset any immediate worry on Wall Street.

Free cash flow is metric that details how much money is left over after a company pays for operations and investments. So, over the last year, Amazon has spent significantly more money that it has brought in.

Chief executive Andy Jassy boasted 37% growth in Amazon's Amazon Web Service (AWS) cloud business, noting it was the segment's best showing in four years.

Overall, Amazon's sales grew 20% compared to a year ago, to $200bn, while its profits more than doubled over the same period to hit $63bn.

Forrester analyst Tracy Woo said the growth in Amazon's cloud business was impressive and its combined company results were "a clear indicator that its infrastructure investments are meeting market demand rather than outpacing it."

The company's expectation that it will spend $220b this year on AI, up from a planned $200b just three months ago, did give Woo some slight concern over how successful such ongoing and ever-growing spending will be in the years ahead.

"The bigger question is whether long-term commitments, capacity, power, leases, and guarantees will continue to be a source of economic exposure when capacity comes online in 2027 and 2028," Woo said.

Some tech shares are plunging - what does that mean for the AI revolution?

difficult_sentences.sentence: Shares in the company fell in after-hours trading by more than 7%, even as it showed a 16% increase in revenue to $109b (£81b) thanks in part to unexpectedly high iPhone sales, and a 26% increase in profits to $29b.
difficult_sentences.explanation_zh: 主句为“Shares fell”，“even as”引导让步状语从句，表示对比，即尽管营收和利润增长，股价仍下跌。从句中“thanks in part to”作原因状语。
difficult_sentences.grammar_point: 让步状语从句 (concessive clause with 'even as')
difficult_sentences.translation_zh: 该公司股价在盘后交易中下跌超过7%，尽管其营收增长了16%至1090亿美元，部分得益于意外强劲的iPhone销售，利润也增长了26%至290亿美元。

difficult_sentences.sentence: Outgoing chief executive Tim Cook said while the impact of supply constraints had already shown up with the availability of Mac computers, it was expected to worsen and spread to affect iPhone and iPad products.
difficult_sentences.explanation_zh: 主句为“Tim Cook said”，后接宾语从句。宾语从句中“while”引导让步状语从句，表示“虽然”，主句为“it was expected to worsen and spread”。
difficult_sentences.grammar_point: 宾语从句中的让步状语从句 ('while' clause within reported speech)
difficult_sentences.translation_zh: 即将离任的首席执行官蒂姆·库克表示，虽然供应限制的影响已在Mac电脑的可获得性上显现，但预计会恶化并蔓延至iPhone和iPad产品。

difficult_sentences.sentence: Devices such as Macs and iPhones require microprocessors with "advanced nodes" - essentially computer chip technology that allows them to operate more quickly - most of which Apple has manufactured through TSMC, which is based in Taiwan.
difficult_sentences.explanation_zh: 主句为“Devices require microprocessors”。破折号内为“advanced nodes”的同位语解释；“most of which”引导非限制性定语从句修饰“microprocessors”；“which is based in Taiwan”为非限制性定语从句修饰“TSMC”。
difficult_sentences.grammar_point: 同位语及多重定语从句 (appositive and multiple relative clauses)
difficult_sentences.translation_zh: Mac和iPhone等设备需要配备“先进节点”的微处理器——本质上是能让设备运行更快的计算机芯片技术——其中大部分由苹果通过台积电制造，台积电位于台湾。

difficult_sentences.sentence: Despite showing free cash flow of negative $7.6bn due to massive and ongoing spending on AI projects, Amazon's core businesses grew enough to offset any immediate worry on Wall Street.
difficult_sentences.explanation_zh: “Despite”引导让步介词短语，包含分词结构“showing ...”；主句为“Amazon's core businesses grew enough ...”，“to offset any immediate worry”作结果状语。
difficult_sentences.grammar_point: 介词短语中的分句结构与不定式表结果 (participial phrase with 'despite' and infinitive of result)
difficult_sentences.translation_zh: 尽管因大规模持续的AI项目支出而录得负76亿美元的自由现金流，亚马逊的核心业务增长足以抵消华尔街的任何即时担忧。

idioms.usage_note: 用作插入语，表明接下来要说的是实话，常用于口语和商务场合。
idioms.example: To be candid, I think the proposal needs more work before it can be approved.

idioms.meaning_zh: 如果你愿意这样说的话，可以说
idioms.usage_note: 用来表明所使用的词语可能不寻常或比喻性，是一种语用标记。
idioms.example: These findings represent, if you will, a paradigm shift in our understanding of the disease.

idioms.meaning_zh: 竞争武器，比喻在商业竞争中的优势工具
idioms.usage_note: 商业比喻，常指技术、策略等能帮助公司获得竞争优势的东西。
idioms.example: The company viewed its proprietary data as a competitive weapon against rivals.

idioms.meaning_zh: 更大的问题，用于引入更重要的议题
idioms.usage_note: 常用于分析或评论中，将讨论转向更深层或更关键的问题。
idioms.example: The product launch went smoothly, but the bigger question is whether it will attract enough buyers.

reading_questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.A: Apple warns of significant supply constraints, causing shares to fall, whereas Amazon’s robust cloud growth eases worries about its heavy AI investments.
options.B: Apple’s strong iPhone sales offset supply chain concerns, while Amazon’s aggressive AI spending raises doubts.
options.C: Both Apple and Amazon face supply chain disruptions and increased competition in AI, weighing on their stock performance.
options.D: Apple’s CEO change and Amazon’s free cash flow issues are the primary concerns for investors in the tech sector.

reading_questions.question: According to Tim Cook, what was the core issue behind Apple’s supply constraints?

options.A: Limited flexibility in the supply chain.

reading_questions.question: What can be inferred about the release of the new version of Siri in the European Union?

options.C: It will be available simultaneously with other regions.
options.D: It faces technical hurdles due to AI regulations.

reading_questions.question: The word "spooked" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
What is the author’s overall attitude toward the companies discussed?
How is the passage primarily organized?

options.B: Sequential reporting of earnings calls with analyst commentary.
options.C: Cause-and-effect analysis of supply chain issues.
options.D: Problem-solution structure focusing on AI investments.

reading_questions.question: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?

options.A: Divergent Fortunes in Tech: Apple’s Supply Fears, Amazon’s AI Bet
options.D: The AI Revolution’s Impact on Tech Stocks

sources.title: Apple warns of future 'supply constraints' for Mac, iPhone, iPad
